metaDescription: Six benchtop drill presses compared on swing size, motor type, speed range, spindle travel and table design, for woodworking and metal drilling.
expertTake: The JET JWDP-12 is the drill press for a serious woodworking bench, with a 12 inch swing, 3-1/8 inch spindle travel and speed changes without moving a belt. The WEN DP1062V is the value pick, adding a digital RPM readout to a 10 inch cast iron machine. If you only drill small holes in thin stock, a floor model is wasted space and a good benchtop is all you need.
introParagraphs: A drill press holds the bit perfectly square to the table and feeds it through the work with a lever, which is why it drills a cleaner, straighter hole than any handheld drill. The numbers on the box, though, rarely say how much runout, table flex or speed range you are really buying.
This guide explains swing, spindle travel, induction motors and speed control, and where cheap presses cut corners.

products.name: JET JWDP-12 12 Inch Benchtop Drill Press with Digital RPM
products.description:
The JET JWDP-12 uses a speed lever that changes spindle speed while the motor runs, so you never open the head to move a belt. A 12 inch swing means the bit reaches 6 inches from the column, which handles wide panels and cabinet parts. Spindle travel is 3-1/8 inches, deeper than the 2 inch travel on the WEN DP1062V.

A 5/8 inch chuck capacity opens up larger bits for woodworking. The cast iron base and tilting table add rigidity, and a laser crosshair and LED light help alignment. Compared with the JET JWDP-10 it has more swing, a larger chuck and a stronger motor.

It is heavy, so choose a sturdy bench. Wax the column and table to keep them sliding and check the chuck for runout once a year. Add a fence and a sacrificial table board to make repeatable holes in cabinet parts.
products.bestFor: Woodworkers who want a precise, flexible benchtop press.
pros: Speed changes without touching a belt
3-1/8 inch spindle travel for deep holes
Cast iron base and table add stability
cons: Heavy to move around a shop
1/2 HP is modest for large metal bits
Costs more than VEVOR and WEN

products.name: WEN DP1062V 10 Inch Variable Speed Benchtop Drill Press
products.description:
The WEN DP1062V uses a 6.2 amp induction motor with mechanical variable speed from 530 to 3,100 rpm. A digital readout shows the actual speed, which helps match speeds to bit size. Its cast iron build and 10 inch swing suit general shop use.

Compared with the JET JWDP-12 it has a smaller swing and 2 inch spindle travel, which limits deep holes. Against the Skil DP9505-00 it offers continuous speed adjustment instead of five fixed steps. It is a good fit for hobbyists who want a speed readout at a modest price.

Because the speed control is mechanical, change speed only with the motor running. Keep the table clean and oil the column occasionally. The readout is only helpful if you actually set speed by it, so keep a chart on the wall.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists who want variable speed and a readout at low cost.
cons: 10 inch swing is smaller than the JET
Brand support is lighter than JET

products.name: JET JWDP-10 10 Inch Benchtop Drill Press
products.description:
The JET JWDP-10 gives a 10 inch swing and five speeds from 630 to 3,300 rpm, changed by moving a belt. A 1/3 HP, 6.2 amp motor drives a JT33 chuck that accepts bits from 1/16 to 1/2 inch. The table tilts plus or minus 45 degrees for angled holes.

Compared with the JET JWDP-12 it has a smaller swing and no lever speed change. Against the WEN DP1062V it uses fixed belt speeds but comes from a brand with strong support. It is a straightforward, durable press for a home shop.

Belt speed changes take a minute, so plan your work by speed. Check belt tension and keep the chuck clean. Use the tilt stops to set repeatable angles for dowel work.
products.bestFor: Home shops that value brand support and durability.
pros: Five speeds cover wood and metal
cons: Belt changes are slower than lever systems

products.name: Skil DP9505-00 10 Inch 5-Speed Benchtop Drill Press
products.description:
The Skil DP9505-00 has a 6.2 amp induction motor with five speeds from 610 to 2,800 rpm and a laser alignment guide. A work light brightens the table. It is a practical entry level press.

Its top speed of 2,800 rpm is a little lower than the WEN or JET 10 inch models, and speed changes are by belt. Compared with the QD-Kyoho 8 inch it is larger and stronger. It suits general wood and light metal drilling.

The laser is helpful, but verify its alignment before trusting it. Wipe the table and column regularly. A shop vacuum nozzle near the table keeps chips from the laser lens.
products.bestFor: Beginners who want a laser guide and five fixed speeds.
pros: Laser guide helps line up holes
cons: Top speed lower than some rivals

products.name: VEVOR 12 Inch 1 HP Variable Speed Benchtop Drill Press
products.description:
The VEVOR 12 inch press quotes 1.0 HP from a 6.2 amp motor, with variable speed from 530 to 3,140 rpm, a digital readout and an X-laser guide. The table tilts 0 to 45 degrees. On paper it matches the JET JWDP-12 on swing and offers more motor power at a lower price.

A horsepower figure on a 120V tool should be read as a peak claim, since a 6.2 amp draw is the real limit. Compared with the WEN DP1062V it has a bigger swing and the same variable speed concept. The JET still wins on build and support.

Check the table for flatness and runout when you unpack it, and plan to shim or adjust if needed. Keep the vents clear. Tighten the column lock bolt before every job, since a loose head spoils accuracy.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists who want a 12 inch swing at a lower cost.
pros: 12 inch swing at a low price
Variable speed with a digital readout
cons: Horsepower claim is a peak figure

products.name: QD-KYOHO 8 Inch 5-Speed Benchtop Drill Press with Vise
products.description:
The QD-Kyoho press has an 8 inch swing and a 300 W motor with five preset speeds starting at 620 rpm. A precision vise with 2-1/2 inch jaws is included, and the head is cast iron. It is the smallest press here.

It will not match the JET JWDP-12 for depth or power, but it takes little bench space. It suits small parts, jewelry, models and light wood. Compared with the Skil DP9505-00 it has a smaller motor.

It is a good second press for small jobs. Check the chuck and vise for play, and oil the column. Use the vise on every small part, never hold the work by hand.
products.bestFor: Small shops and hobbyists drilling small parts.
pros: Compact 8 inch swing saves bench space
cons: 300 W motor is the weakest here

buyingCriteria.explanation: Swing is twice the distance from the column to the bit center. A 10 inch press reaches 5 inches in from the edge, and a 12 inch press reaches 6 inches. The JET JWDP-12 and VEVOR 12 inch let you drill further into wide boards. Pick a swing that matches your widest workpiece. The mistake is buying a small swing and then trying to drill the center of a 14 inch panel. Measure your widest board first, and divide by two.

Induction motors are quiet and durable, and a 6.2 amp motor like the WEN DP1062V is typical for benchtop presses. Horsepower claims can mislead, so check the amp rating. A 300 W motor like the QD-Kyoho suits small work. Large bits need more power. Compare amps, not horsepower: a 120V tool cannot truly deliver more than about 6.2 amps on a standard circuit without tripping it, so 1 HP claims are peak numbers.

Big bits need slow speeds, and small bits need fast speeds. The JET JWDP-12 changes speed by lever while running, and the WEN offers 530 to 3,100 rpm. Belt changes on the JET JWDP-10 and Skil take longer. If you change speed often, choose a variable system. As a rule of thumb, drill steel under 500 rpm for bits over 1/2 inch and use cutting oil. Wood and small bits can run well above 2,000 rpm.

Travel is how far the chuck can descend, and it limits hole depth. The JET JWDP-12 has 3-1/8 inches, while the WEN has 2 inches. For deep holes in thick stock, more travel matters. Check the travel against your thickest piece. Counterbore and mortise work need travel too, so thick stock calls for 3 inches or more. A short quill forces you to raise the table mid job.

A flat, stiff table keeps holes square. Cast iron tables on the JET and WEN resist flex. Runout is the wobble of the bit, and it spoils precision. Check it with a dial indicator or a straight rod. A cheap table that flexes will tilt a hole by a degree or two under pressure. Press down on the table edge and look for movement.

JET provides parts and service, while budget brands often lack support. A press lasts decades, so a spare belt and chuck matter. The VEVOR offers more power per dollar but weaker support. Decide how much you value long term backup. A spare belt, chuck and key cost little but save weeks of downtime. Ask whether the brand stocks them before you buy.

specDecoder.meaning: Twice the throat distance from the column to the chuck center. A 10 inch swing means 5 inches of reach. It sets the widest panel you can center a hole in.
specDecoder.watchFor: Some makers quote overall width, not throat.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum distance the quill moves, 3-1/8 inches on the JET JWDP-12. It sets hole depth in one pass.
specDecoder.watchFor: Travel is less than bit length, so deep holes need a lift.

specDecoder.meaning: A brushless AC motor that is quiet and has no brushes to wear. The WEN DP1062V and Skil use them.
specDecoder.watchFor: Horsepower claims often exceed what the amp rating supports.

specDecoder.meaning: The wobble of the chuck axis. Lower runout gives cleaner holes. It is rarely listed.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check it yourself with a straight rod and a dial indicator.

specDecoder.meaning: The largest bit shank the chuck holds, such as 5/8 inch on the JET JWDP-12 or 1/2 inch on the JWDP-10.
specDecoder.watchFor: A bigger chuck does not mean a stronger motor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared swing, spindle travel and chuck size, with the JET JWDP-12 at 12 inches, 3-1/8 inches and 5/8 inch leading. Larger capacity meant a wider range of work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at amp ratings and speed ranges, including 530 to 3,100 rpm on the WEN. Variable speed earned more credit than fixed belts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We rewarded cast iron bases, tables and heads. Presses with rigid tables ranked higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Features
howWeEvaluated.description: Digital readouts, laser guides and lights were considered. The WEN readout and Skil laser were credited.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The JET JWDP-12 leads on build, the WEN on value and the VEVOR on power per dollar. The QD-Kyoho serves small shops.

cards.label: Variable speed
cards.text: Speed changes with a lever or knob while running. The JET JWDP-12, WEN DP1062V and VEVOR 12 inch fit here. They suit frequent changes.

cards.label: Belt speed
cards.text: Speed changes by moving a belt on pulleys. The JET JWDP-10, Skil DP9505-00 and QD-Kyoho fit here. They are simpler and cheap.

howToChoose.note: Choose variable if you switch between wood and metal often.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Slow speeds, a stiff table and a vise. Metal needs low rpm and cutting oil. A larger motor helps.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The JET JWDP-12 and VEVOR 12 inch offer the most power. The QD-Kyoho vise helps hold small metal parts.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use the press weekly or want it to last decades. The JET JWDP-12 repays the cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You drill occasionally. The WEN DP1062V or Skil DP9505-00 is enough.

maintenance.why: Rust and dust make the quill stick. A paste wax keeps it smooth.
A loose belt slips under load. A tight belt strains bearings.
Runout ruins hole accuracy. Replace the chuck if it wobbles.
A dry quill binds. A light oil keeps it moving.
Dust blocks cooling air. Overheating shortens motor life.

faq.a: A 10 inch swing suits most home shops. A 12 inch swing handles wider boards. Choose based on your widest workpiece.
Benchtop presses save space and suit most hobby work. Floor presses give more travel and power.
Use slow speeds for large bits and cutting oil. Faster speeds suit small bits in wood.
No. A laser is a convenience, and it must be aligned. A scribed mark and a center punch work too.
For large bits, yes. For small work, a 300 W motor is fine.

faq.q: Can I use a drill press as a sander?
faq.a: Yes, with drum sanding attachments. Use low speeds and a table insert.
